transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Lately I just don’t care about the art shows, the mentoring, or even my photography anymore; nothing feels worth doing. My wife persuaded me to come in after I recently missed a major exhibition opening I had organized, because I just couldn't bring myself to go.
Have you had other periods in your life, lasting at least two weeks, when you felt similarly down or lost interest in things? If so, about how many times has this happened before?
No, I’ve never experienced periods of depression or loss of interest like this before in my life. These feelings and the intense mood swings only began after I retired from my job.

Do your low mood and loss of interest happen mainly when you’re thinking about or dealing with your retirement, or are they present most of the day even when you’re not focused on retirement? About how long have these symptoms been going on?

This heavy, joyless feeling is there all the time, constantly hanging over me no matter what I'm thinking about. It has been going on for most of the past year, starting right after my high-energy period fizzled out. It has really disrupted my life for about the last five months now.

When you feel this depressed, have you ever heard or seen things other people couldn’t, or become convinced of something like being ruined, guilty, or beyond help even when others said it wasn’t true?

No, I’ve never seen or heard things that weren't there. But I do feel deeply guilty, constantly replaying old missteps from my career and marriage as if they're unforgivable sins. I just feel like a useless fraud, even though my wife tells me that's not true.

When you feel like a useless fraud or that your past mistakes are unforgivable, do you believe these things with absolute certainty even when others try to reassure you, or do you recognize they may be part of your depression?

I definitely feel like a fraud and keep replaying those mistakes, but I’m not entirely sure how to answer about my level of certainty. In the moment, it all feels completely real and true, and I haven't really thought about whether it's just the depression talking.

When those thoughts come up, are you completely convinced they are true no matter what anyone says, or can you step back and recognize they might be exaggerated by your depression? Has this ever led you to think you deserve punishment or that you’ve caused irreversible ruin?

When I'm in the thick of it, I am completely convinced those thoughts are true and I can't step back to see them as exaggerated. I truly feel like a useless old fraud, replaying past missteps in my career and marriage as if they are unforgivable, irreversible sins. It gets so heavy that I genuinely believe everyone would be better off if I just disappeared.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports bipolar affective disorder, current episode severe depression with psychotic symptoms. The patient describes a prior distinct high-energy period followed by a prolonged depressive episode with pervasive anhedonia and low mood. During depression, he has mood-congruent psychotic guilt/worthlessness beliefs held with delusional conviction ('unforgivable, irreversible sins,' 'useless old fraud,' others better off if he disappeared), without hallucinations. Symptoms are persistent and functionally impairing.
